cases.name: Janet Swallow
cases.about: Diego Demelo, a friend of Swallow, said, "Janet always smiled and mentored new nurses, mentored myself. It's really tragic to hear this." Swallow leaves behind two sons. In a GoFundMe page, loved ones raved about her "kindness, presence, and love for her family." She worked at Lahey Hospital & Medical Center, where Chief Nursing Officer Scott James remembered her as "a beloved and valued member" of the team.
cases.narrative:
On 3/12/2026, she was found murdered in her home. Prosecutors said DeMayo climbed into the woman’s window and fatally stabbed her while she was in bed.

The death investigation began after Lynn police received a 911 call from a resident reporting a young man with a knife walking along Standard Street. "It was like a 6-inch blade, and he was just swinging his arm around, and then he just started stabbing all the bushes. And it looked like he was pretending the bushes were a person. It was like he was practicing," 911 caller Ashley O'Brien said. "It was the most bizarre thing I ever seen." Rhonda Deparolesa, a neighbor, recounted the incident, saying, "I knew he had something in his hand, but I didn't know what it was, but my husband said it was a knife and it had blood on it." She added, "And he tried to open my door, but I lock my doors."
